verification_report.summary:
Every supplied statement and deduction passes the independent audit. The normalization omega=i/(2pi)g gives exactly h=g+u_{i bar j}, Delta_g u=S-n, Delta_h u=n-B and det(h)/det(g)=e^G; no additional 2pi factor enters. The calculation and estimates require no closedness, BMP or PVP. Connectedness is harmlessly redundant for these a priori bounds.

The two torsion switches give precisely the displayed E. The first produces (nabla_i overline(T_{jl}^q))(g_{k bar q}-h_{k bar q})-overline(T_{jl}^q)nabla_i h_{k bar q}; commuting in the specified order contributes +C_{i bar l k bar j}. The second produces (nabla_bar l T_{ik}^p)(g_{p bar j}-h_{p bar j})-T_{ik}^p nabla_bar l h_{p bar j}. Switching the remaining first-switch derivative contributes +T_{ik}^p overline(T_{jl}^q)(h_{p bar q}-g_{p bar q}). The two derivative terms are conjugates after contraction. Thus E is exactly the contraction by h^{i bar j}g^{k bar l} of the two stated differentiated-torsion terms, +C, and -T_{ik}^p overline(T_{jl}^q)g_{p bar q}. With R_{i bar l k}^p=-partial_bar l Gamma_{ik}^p, C=-R_{i bar l k}^p h_{p bar j}+overline(R_{l bar i j}^q)h_{k bar q}. It has no derivatives of h. In a g-unitary diagonal frame its coefficients are bounded by C_g(1+S), and contraction gives |E|<=C_g(1+S)B.

The positive norms and cross terms also agree exactly. In that frame, ||A||^2=sum |A_{ik bar j}|^2/(lambda_k lambda_j) and ||D||^2=sum (lambda_p/lambda_k)|T_{ik}^p|^2. Interchanging i,k identifies the latter with the positive torsion-product contribution, and torsion antisymmetry converts the derivative cross term to +2 Re<A,D>. Differentiating the determinant gives the displayed Delta_g G identity, hence Delta_h S=||A+D||^2+Delta_g G+E. The torsion switch gives g^{i bar l}(A+D)_{ik bar l}=S_k+tau_k. Direct contraction gives ||H||^2=|partial S|_h^2/S and <A+D,H>=h^{k bar q}(S_k+tau_k)S_bar q/S. Expanding K therefore gives precisely the supplied square and residual torsion trace, with their stated signs and factors. The exact logarithmic identity follows, and E/S>=-2C_g B when S>=1 proves the lemma.

All cases of the maximum argument are valid. Compactness supplies a maximum of Q. Its maximum property always gives S(y)<=S(x)exp(AD+1), handling S(x)<1 immediately. At S(x)>=1, SB>=n^2 implies Delta_g G/S>=-KB/n^2, and partial Q=0 gives S_k/S=(A+s^{-2})u_k. Cauchy-Schwarz and weighted Young give exactly the displayed torsion absorption. If S(x)^2<=(A+1)^2(D+1)^3 the trace is already bounded. Otherwise the residual Young coefficient is bounded by C_g independently of A,D. Differentiating Q leaves a nonnegative gradient term and yields 0>=(A-C_g-K/n^2)B-n(A+1). Choosing A>C_g+K/n^2+1 is non-circular and bounds B(x). For n>=2, S(x)<=n e^K B(x)^{n-1}; for n=1, S=e^G. Propagation gives S<=C(g,D,K). Finally, lambda_i=e^G/product_{j!=i}lambda_j>=e^{-K}C^{-(n-1)}, proving the lower metric bound as well as the upper one.

The regularity reduction stays within the accepted inputs. The fixed Delta_g estimate bounds W^{2,p}(u) from its bounded trace and C0 norm; Sobolev embedding in real dimension 2n gives C^{1,alpha} for every alpha<1. To verify the claimed extension explicitly, place h in ell I<=h<=L I on fixed coordinate charts and set fhat(Y)=inf_{ell I<=N<=L I}[log det N+tr(N^{-1}(Y-N))]. Supporting-plane concavity makes this a finite concave extension agreeing with log det on the required range. For P>=0, its increments lie between tr(P)/L and tr(P)/ell. The complex-Hessian map Lc satisfies Lc(M)>=0 for real M>=0 and tr_C Lc(M)=tr_R(M)/4 in z=x+iy coordinates; the real J-invariant projection itself preserves real trace. Consequently fhat(g(x)+Lc(M)) is uniformly elliptic on all real symmetric matrices, with constants 1/(4L),1/(4ell), and its x oscillation is controlled by the fixed smooth g independently of M. Standard local concave Evans-Krylov applies and gives C^{2,beta} for some uniform beta>0, without presupposing a bound for the full real Hessian. Differentiation then gives linear equations with uniformly elliptic Holder coefficients; Schauder induction and a finite chart cover give every higher bound. No stronger geometric regularity input is necessary.

For the final extension, a is a spatially constant parameter in [0,a_max], as stated. Bounded u and F bound |a u+F|, while Delta_g(a u+F)>=-a_max n+Delta_g F supplies the required lower bound without prior derivative estimates for u. After the second estimate and fixed-operator estimate, a u+F has controlled C^{1,alpha} norm, so the same Evans-Krylov step applies. For v=partial_r u the differentiated equation is (h^{i bar j}partial_i partial_bar j-a)v=partial_r F+partial_r log det g-h^{i bar j}partial_r g_{i bar j}. Schauder induction therefore closes uniformly for the entire interval, including a=0; no positive lower bound on a or proper-equation existence result is used.

Attribution was checked by arXiv theorem search first, followed by web search and direct comparison with the supplied TW15 text. The theorem search returned no matching statement; the supplied source and web record identify [Tosatti-Weinkove, arXiv:1201.0312](https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.0312). Section 3 contains the torsion completion and Section 9 the relevant maximum argument in the proof of (9.3). Theorem 9.1 itself is a C0 theorem and was not used. All tensor identities and estimates above were verified independently.
